name: introduction to obesity overview
title: Obesity management by body mass index: lifestyle and psychology for everyone; a drug (tirzepatide or semaglutide first, naltrexone-bupropion next) at BMI 30, or 27 with complications; bariatric surgery at BMI 40, 35 with a complication, or 30 with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes; each column gives what to check before, what to give, and what to expect or watch

nodes.title: Obesity: how far up the ladder? BMI + complications decide
lines: body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30, or ≥ 25 South or East Asian · always with waist circumference
ASK permission first · ASSESS the 4 M's (mental, mechanical, metabolic, monetary)
rule out hypothyroidism, Cushing's, medications · A1c, lipids, thyroid-stimulating hormone, alanine aminotransferase

nodes.title: EVERYONE, whatever the BMI
lines: goal: health and well-being, not a number

nodes.title: BMI ≥ 30, or ≥ 27 with complications: ADD A DRUG
lines: ≥ 5% loss by 12 weeks at the maximum tolerated dose, else switch · likely lifelong

nodes.title: BMI ≥ 40, ≥ 35 + a complication, or ≥ 30 + poorly controlled type 2 diabetes: SURGERY
Lifestyle + psychology
lines: the base under every other step

nodes.title: Tirzepatide > semaglutide
lines: glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) agonists; tirzepatide adds glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)
the most effective drugs

nodes.title: Naltrexone-bupropion
lines: one oral tablet
orlistat: rarely, weak + side effects

nodes.title: Bariatric surgery
lines: sleeve or Roux-en-Y bypass most common
gastric band: no longer done

nodes.title: Agree on SMART goals
lines: • prevent gain, or lose weight?
• readiness: motivational interviewing
• cardiology referral before exercise, if needed

nodes.title: NOT in pregnancy
lines: other cautions: see the GLUCOSE-LOWERING DRUGS tree

nodes.title: NOT if ANY of these
lines: • pregnancy, any OPIOID use, monoamine oxidase inhibitor
• seizure history or risk
• uncontrolled hypertension, renal or liver failure

nodes.title: NOT a candidate if
lines: • unstable psychiatric illness, untreated substance use
• malignancy, short life expectancy
• can't keep up follow-up

nodes.title: MUST first
lines: • stop smoking, for good
• treat mental health conditions

nodes.title: The three foundations
lines: • healthy eating, ideally with a dietitian
• activity 30–60 min most days + resistance
• sleep, stress, cognitive behavioural therapy

nodes.title: Weekly injection, up every 4 weeks
lines: • tirzepatide to 15 mg: −20.9%
• semaglutide to 2.4 mg: −12.4%

nodes.title: Build up to 2 tablets twice daily
lines: −4.8% on average

nodes.title: 25–30% loss · ↓ long-term mortality
lines: type 2 diabetes, fatty liver, polycystic ovary syndrome, sleep apnea improve or remit

nodes.title: Losing? 0.5–1 kg a week
lines: activity: little loss, but keeps it off

nodes.title: Slows gastric emptying
lines: absorption of other drugs changes, e.g. the pill

nodes.title: Deficiencies, worst after Roux-en-Y
lines: • protein: 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day
• iron, B12, calcium + vitamin D, vitamin A

nodes.title: THIAMINE before any glucose
lines: Wernicke's: 1–3 months post-op, nausea, poor intake
